previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, atrial fibrillation, and prior drug-induced thrombocytopenia was admitted for worsening thrombocytopenia with a platelet count of 29,000. She reported a new petechial rash and discoloration of stool, though the latter was likely due to recent beet consumption. Workup ruled out active infections including CMV, HIV, hepatitis, and EBV. A bone marrow biopsy was performed to evaluate for myelodysplastic syndrome or immune thrombocytopenia, with results pending at discharge. She was started on a two-week course of prednisone as a trial for ITP. Warfarin was held during admission due to bleeding risk but was to be restarted upon platelet recovery. She remained asymptomatic throughout, with stable vital signs and no bleeding complications. She was discharged home with close hematology follow-up planned within one week and instructions to monitor weight and complete outpatient lab testing.

instability, a family meeting was held and the decision was made 
to proceed with comfort-focused care. Pressors with withdrawn, a 
morphine drip was started, and the patient died peacefully.
